facts.fact: A Microsoft 365 Copilot plugin is an installable package that can contain declarative agents, skills, Copilot connector configuration and references to remote MCP servers; the package holds connection information for an MCP server, but the server runs separately (overview page dated 2026-11-02) (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/plugins-overview)
The Microsoft 365 Copilot extensibility docs now centre on 'plugins' as the installable package (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/plugins-overview)

'Plugin' has two meanings: the customer-facing plugin package, and 'MCP and API plugins', the technical custom actions inside a declarative agent, which aren't enabled as standalone experiences in Microsoft 365 Copilot (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/overview-plugins)

Declarative agents can call remote MCP servers as actions; for MCP plugins Copilot discovers tools dynamically at runtime by default, or a developer can pin a fixed tool set in the plugin manifest (page dated 2026-11-06) (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/overview-plugins)

Declarative agents can call OpenAPI-described REST APIs as actions, and REST API plugins always use the tools defined in the manifest (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/overview-plugins)

Dynamic tool discovery for an MCP server declared through `agentConnectors` needs Microsoft 365 app manifest version 1.29 or later and a host that permits it (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/overview-plugins)

MCP plugins can return interactive UI widgets ('MCP apps') built with the OpenAI Apps SDK, rendered inline or full-screen in Microsoft 365 Copilot (announced March 2026) (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/whats-new ; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/overview-plugins)
API plugins use Adaptive Card templates instead of MCP app widgets (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/overview-plugins)

Declarative agent manifest schema 1.9 (October 2026) adds a top-level `agent_skills` property (skill directories that follow the Agent Skills standard) and a `Fabric` capability, and makes `instructions` optional (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/whats-new)

Declarative agent manifest version 1.8 (July 2026) added the `EmailActions` and `MeetingActions` capabilities, and version 1.7 (May 2026) added `editorial_answers` and `default_response_mode` (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/whats-new)
The `agent_skills` property in manifest schema 1.9 points to skill directories that follow the Agent Skills standard (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/whats-new)

Skills in Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat have been GA since November 2026; a skill is a set of reusable task instructions with optional resources and scripts, usable in Chat without a declarative agent, and distributable through plugin packages (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/whats-new)

Custom engine agents bring their own orchestrator and model and can be built with Copilot Studio, the Microsoft 365 Agents SDK, the Teams SDK or Microsoft Foundry (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/overview-custom-engine-agent)
Custom engine agents require Microsoft 365 app manifest version 1.21 or later (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/overview-custom-engine-agent)

The Microsoft 365 Agents SDK is one of the tools (with Copilot Studio, the Teams SDK and Microsoft Foundry) for building custom engine agents (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/overview-custom-engine-agent)

Pro-code custom engine agents reach M365 data through Microsoft Graph and the Copilot Retrieval API, while Copilot Studio agents have native access to Microsoft 365 and Copilot connector content (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/overview-custom-engine-agent)

Agent evaluation tooling for M365 agents, the Microsoft 365 Copilot Evaluations CLI and an evaluation framework, has existed since May 2026 (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/whats-new)

The Copilot APIs are REST APIs under the Microsoft Graph `copilot` namespace at `graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/copilot` and `graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot`, using the same Entra authentication as other Graph APIs (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/copilot-apis-overview)
The Copilot APIs require a Microsoft 365 Copilot license for each calling user (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/copilot-apis-overview)

The Copilot API list as of 2026-11-02 has nine entries: the Retrieval API (no preview label), the Search API (preview), the Chat API (preview), the Interaction Export API, AI Interactions Change Notifications (preview), the Meeting Insights API, Copilot usage reports, the Package Management API and the Cost Management API (preview) (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/copilot-apis-overview)
The Copilot Search API is in preview as of 2026-11-02 (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/copilot-apis-overview)
The Copilot Cost Management API is in preview as of 2026-11-02 (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/copilot-apis-overview)
The Interaction Export API is one of the nine Copilot APIs listed as of 2026-11-02 (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/copilot-apis-overview)
The Package Management API is one of the nine Copilot APIs listed as of 2026-11-02 (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/copilot-apis-overview)

The Retrieval API returns text chunks for RAG from the M365 Copilot hybrid index, with sources SharePoint, OneDrive and Copilot connectors and KQL filtering through `filterExpression` (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/api/ai-services/retrieval/overview)
The Copilot Retrieval API was announced GA on 2025-11-20 (https://devblogs.microsoft.com/microsoft365dev/microsoft-365-copilot-apis-whats-new-and-whats-next/)
SharePoint is a Retrieval API source, along with OneDrive and Copilot connectors (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/api/ai-services/retrieval/overview)

facts.fact: The Retrieval API is also sold pay-as-you-go to users without a Copilot license, in preview since January 2026, covering tenant-level sources only (SharePoint and Copilot connectors), not OneDrive (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/api/ai-services/retrieval/overview)

The Chat API (preview) runs multi-turn conversations with M365 Copilot grounded in enterprise search and web search, with a synchronous `chat` endpoint and an SSE `chatOverStream` endpoint; it returns text only and doesn't perform actions (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/api/ai-services/chat/overview)
The Copilot Chat API requires a Copilot add-on license (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/api/ai-services/chat/overview)

Work IQ is Microsoft's workplace intelligence layer for agents, offering chat, context, tools and workspaces over A2A, remote MCP, local MCP and REST (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/work-iq/)
Work IQ is reachable over A2A as well as remote MCP, local MCP and REST (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/work-iq/)
Work IQ is reachable over remote MCP and local MCP (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/work-iq/)

Work IQ usage is billed per use in Copilot Credits independent of Microsoft 365 Copilot licensing; Copilot-licensed users are still billed per use when custom or third-party agents call it (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/work-iq/ ; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/work-iq/api-overview)
Work IQ context also includes Dynamics 365 and Power Platform business data, not just M365 productivity data (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/work-iq/)
Work IQ became GA on 2026-06-16 (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/work-iq/cli)

Work IQ Workspaces gives agents persistent working storage for long-running workflows on SharePoint Embedded inside the tenant boundary (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/work-iq/)

Copilot Studio agents run on one of three harnesses (Microsoft Copilot, Customer Conversation, standard), and the harness determines features and billing (page dated 2026-10-19) (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/harnesses-overview)

The Microsoft Copilot harness is for reasoning-heavy, multistep work and has skills, memory, file creation and a sandbox (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/harnesses-overview)
The Customer Conversation harness is for voice and chat customer service with human escalation (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/harnesses-overview)
The standard harness covers classic topics, rule-based agents and agent flows (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/harnesses-overview)
The Microsoft Copilot harness became a 'production-ready preview' in June 2026 (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/whats-new)
The Customer Conversation harness went into preview in October 2026 (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/whats-new)

Since October 2026 (preview), Copilot Studio can upgrade an agent from the standard harness to the Microsoft Copilot harness, rebuilding topics as skills or workflows (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/whats-new)

GPT-5.5 Chat is the default model on the Copilot Studio standard harness as of October 2026, and became GA as a primary model in June 2026 (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/whats-new)
Claude Opus 4.8 is GA in Copilot Studio as of October 2026 (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/whats-new)

Since October 2026, agents keep their current model for up to 30 days after Copilot Studio moves the default (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/whats-new)

Copilot Studio connected agents went GA over A2A in April 2026, and adding an external A2A agent as a connected agent is in preview (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/whats-new)
Since October 2026, Copilot Studio connected agents can also target Microsoft Foundry agents and Microsoft 365 Agents SDK agents (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/whats-new)

facts.fact: Copilot Studio computer use has been GA since May 2026; agents operate Windows web and desktop apps with a virtual mouse and keyboard (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/computer-use ; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/whats-new)

Computer use requires generative orchestration and is billed per step: 5 Copilot Credits on standard models, 15 on premium models (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/computer-use)
GA computer use models are OpenAI Computer-Using Agent (CUA), OpenAI GPT-6 Sol and Anthropic Claude Sonnet 4.5 (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/computer-use)
OpenAI GPT-6 Sol is a GA computer use model in Copilot Studio (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/computer-use)

Anthropic Claude Sonnet 4.5 is a GA computer use model in Copilot Studio; Anthropic models need the admin setting that allows external models (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/computer-use)
Claude Sonnet 4.6 is experimental for Copilot Studio computer use (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/computer-use)
Claude Opus 4.6 (premium) is experimental for Copilot Studio computer use (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/computer-use)

The Windows 365 for Agents MCP server has been GA since June 2026 and gives agents control of a Windows 365 Cloud PC: desktop interaction, browser automation and UI inspection (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/whats-new)
Cloud PC pooling for computer use went into preview in January 2026 (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/whats-new)

Agent flows (standard harness) are workflows billed in Copilot Credits, not Power Platform requests (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/whats-new ; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/admin/api-request-limits-allocations)

Asynchronous responses (May 2026) let a long-running agent flow exceed the two-minute limit and return results later; there are also an agent node (March 2026), a prompt node and a Microsoft 365 Copilot node (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/whats-new)

Agent evaluations have been GA since March 2026 with multi-turn tests, and a content-safety test method was added in September 2026 (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/whats-new)
Running Copilot Studio evaluations through the Power Platform API REST surface went into preview in April 2026 (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/whats-new)
Environment-level Copilot Studio agent telemetry export to Azure Application Insights went into preview in July 2026 (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/whats-new)
Copilot Studio agents can onboard to Microsoft Agent 365 for centralized observability and governance (August 2026) (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/whats-new)

Memory and skills have been available for Microsoft Copilot harness agents since June 2026; memory stores preferences per user, and skills can be exported as Markdown (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/whats-new)

Dataverse tables became a Copilot Studio knowledge source in September 2026, with unstructured reasoning over text and file columns in preview (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/whats-new)

Copilot Studio knowledge sources gained Azure SQL tables in August 2026 and OneDrive for Business in October 2026, and Fabric IQ and Foundry IQ grounding are in preview (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/whats-new)

Power Apps code apps are code-first web apps (React, Vue and others) hosted on Power Platform that can call 1,500+ connectors from JavaScript (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/code-apps/overview)
An admin must enable code apps per environment (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/code-apps/overview)
End users of code apps need Power Apps Premium, pay-as-you-go, an App Pass or auto-claim (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/code-apps/overview)

Code apps don't support Power Platform Git integration, Power Apps for Windows, SAS IP binding or SharePoint forms integration (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/code-apps/overview)
Desktop flow executions don't consume Power Platform requests (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/admin/api-request-limits-allocations)
Cloud flow triggers and actions consume Power Platform requests at one request each (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/admin/api-request-limits-allocations)

The Work IQ remote MCP endpoint URL is `https://workiq.svc.cloud.microsoft/mcp`, and MCP clients discover its Entra auth through `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/work-iq/mcp/overview)

The Work IQ MCP server works with GitHub Copilot CLI and Foundry, which have Microsoft quickstarts (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/work-iq/mcp/quickstart/github-copilot-cli)
The Work IQ MCP server works with Microsoft Foundry, which has a Microsoft quickstart (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/work-iq/mcp/overview)

Work IQ MCP has 10 generic tools that act on Graph-style resource paths: `fetch`, `fetch_blob`, `create_entity`, `update_entity`, `delete_entity`, `do_action`, `call_function`, `ask`, `retrieve` and `list_agents`, with schema discovery via `get_schema` and `search_paths`; `retrieve` is in public preview (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/work-iq/mcp/overview)

facts.fact: Work IQ's application ID URI is `api://workiq.svc.cloud.microsoft`, with three delegated scopes all requiring admin consent: `WorkIQAgent.Ask`, `WorkIQ.Act` and `WorkIQ.Read` (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/work-iq/permissions)

Work IQ supports on-behalf-of (OBO), while application-only (app-only) auth isn't supported (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/work-iq/permissions ; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/work-iq/api-overview)
An administrator must enable Work IQ in the tenant first (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/work-iq/api-overview)

The Work IQ A2A endpoint accepts JSON-RPC `POST https://workiq.svc.cloud.microsoft/a2a/`, and multi-turn conversations use `contextId` (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/work-iq/api-overview)

The Work IQ A2A endpoint supports A2A v1.0 (header `A2A-Version: 1.0`, method `SendMessage`) and v0.3 (the default) (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/work-iq/api-overview)
Work IQ exposes an A2A JSON-RPC endpoint at `https://workiq.svc.cloud.microsoft/a2a/` (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/work-iq/api-overview)

The Work IQ local MCP server ships in the npm package `@microsoft/workiq` (latest 1.0.1) and runs with `npx -y @microsoft/workiq mcp` (stdio) (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/work-iq/cli ; https://registry.npmjs.org/@microsoft/workiq/latest)
The latest `@microsoft/workiq` npm package version is 1.0.1 (https://registry.npmjs.org/@microsoft/workiq/latest)
There is a GitHub Copilot CLI plugin for Work IQ, installed with `/plugin install workiq@work-iq` (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/work-iq/cli)

The legacy per-workload Microsoft-hosted MCP servers (Copilot, Calendar, Mail, SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams, User and Word, formerly the 'Agent 365 tooling servers') are kept for backward compatibility only, and Microsoft says not to use them in production or new projects (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-agent-365/tooling-servers-overview)
Microsoft says to use Work IQ MCP instead of the legacy per-workload Microsoft-hosted MCP servers (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-agent-365/tooling-servers-overview)

The Dataverse MCP server URL is `https://{org}.crm.dynamics.com/api/mcp` (GA); a preview endpoint, `/api/mcp_preview`, must be enabled per environment (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/maker/data-platform/data-platform-mcp)

Microsoft documents connecting Claude Desktop, Claude Code, GitHub Copilot and Copilot Studio to the Dataverse MCP server (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/maker/data-platform/data-platform-mcp-other-clients)
Claude Desktop is a documented Dataverse MCP client (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/maker/data-platform/data-platform-mcp-other-clients)

Dataverse MCP tools (renamed set) are `search_data`, `search` (now metadata search), `describe`, `read_query` (Dataverse SQL `SELECT`), `create_record`, `update_record`, `delete_record`, `create_table`, `update_table`, `delete_table`, `upsert_skill`, `delete_skill`, `init_file_upload`, `commit_file_upload`, `file_download` and `invoke_api` (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/maker/data-platform/data-platform-mcp)
The older Dataverse MCP tools `list_tables`, `describe_table` and `fetch` were removed (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/maker/data-platform/data-platform-mcp)

Dataverse MCP from Claude goes through the local proxy npm package `@microsoft/dataverse` (latest 1.0.88), for example `claude mcp add dataverse -t stdio -- npx -y @microsoft/dataverse mcp https://yourorg.crm.dynamics.com` (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/maker/data-platform/data-platform-mcp-other-clients ; https://registry.npmjs.org/@microsoft/dataverse/latest)

Before using the local proxy, a tenant admin grants consent to the Dataverse CLI app `0c412cc3-0dd6-449b-987f-05b053db9457`, and that client is enabled in the Power Platform admin center (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/maker/data-platform/data-platform-mcp-other-clients)

To use the remote Dataverse MCP endpoint with your own Entra app, register an app, grant it the Dynamics CRM `mcp.tools` delegated permission, and add its client ID under Power Platform admin center > Environment > Settings > Product > Features > Dataverse Model Context Protocol > Advanced Settings (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/maker/data-platform/data-platform-mcp-other-clients)

Only the Copilot Studio client is enabled for the Dataverse MCP server by default; every non-Microsoft client must be allow-listed per environment by a Power Platform administrator (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/maker/data-platform/data-platform-mcp-disable)
The Dataverse MCP client allow list covers only `/api/mcp`; MCP-named custom APIs are not restricted (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/maker/data-platform/data-platform-mcp-disable)
The Dataverse Web API implements OData v4.0 (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/webapi/overview)

Besides raw HTTP, Microsoft provides the Dataverse SDK for .NET (`ServiceClient`) and a Dataverse SDK for Python (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/webapi/overview ; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/sdk-python/)

The Dataverse SDK for Python is documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/sdk-python/ (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/sdk-python/)
The Microsoft MCP Server for Enterprise (preview) URL is `https://mcp.svc.cloud.microsoft/enterprise` (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/mcp-server/overview)

The Microsoft MCP Server for Enterprise is read-only over Microsoft Entra directory data, with tools `microsoft_graph_suggest_queries`, `microsoft_graph_get` and `microsoft_graph_list_properties` (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/mcp-server/overview)

The Microsoft MCP Server for Enterprise costs nothing extra, is limited to 100 calls per minute per user, and runs in the global cloud only (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/mcp-server/overview)
Microsoft Graph SDKs exist for C#, PowerShell, TypeScript/JavaScript, Java, Go, PHP and Python, and there is also a Graph CLI repo (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/sdks/sdks-overview)
Kiota can generate smaller Graph clients than the full SDKs (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/sdks/sdks-overview)
Microsoft support (CSS) doesn't officially support the Graph SDKs, only the underlying HTTP calls (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/sdks/sdks-overview)
A Graph CLI repo is listed alongside the Microsoft Graph SDKs (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/sdks/sdks-overview)

facts.fact: Copilot Studio agents can call external MCP servers as tools; the only transport supported is Streamable HTTP, and SSE has not been supported since August 2025 (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/mcp-add-existing-server-to-agent)

Copilot Studio MCP tool auth can be none, API key (header or query), or OAuth 2.0 (dynamic discovery with DCR, dynamic, or manual) (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/mcp-add-existing-server-to-agent)

An MCP server can be added as a Power Apps custom connector by importing an OpenAPI 2.0 file whose operation carries `x-ms-agentic-protocol: mcp-streamable-1.0` (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/mcp-add-existing-server-to-agent)
MCP access goes through Power Platform connectors, so DLP data policies govern it (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/mcp-add-existing-server-to-agent)

Copilot Studio agents can be published as a remote MCP server ('MCP client' channel) or an A2A agent ('A2A client' channel) in preview, in early-release environments only (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/publication-channels-mcp-agent-to-agent)

MCP channel clients authenticate with Entra delegated scope `https://api.powerplatform.com/copilotstudio-mcp/MCS.InvokeAsMCP` through an app registration against API app ID `6f46e6ed-07bf-4616-80f0-47546850f654` (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/publication-channels-mcp-agent-to-agent)

A2A channel clients authenticate with Entra delegated scope `https://api.powerplatform.com/copilotstudio-a2a/MCS.InvokeAsA2A` through an app registration against API app ID `6f46e6ed-07bf-4616-80f0-47546850f654` (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/publication-channels-mcp-agent-to-agent)

Copilot Studio MCP is the npm package `@microsoft/copilot-studio-mcp` (latest 1.0.4), launched with `npx -y @microsoft/copilot-studio-mcp@latest` over stdio (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/copilot-studio-mcp ; https://registry.npmjs.org/@microsoft/copilot-studio-mcp/latest)

Copilot Studio MCP lets IDE and CLI clients author and manage agents with tools `discover_resources`, `get_consumption`, `manage_agents`, `manage_workflows` and `get_copilot_studio_skills` (announced October 2026) (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/copilot-studio-mcp)

A custom app sends GET to the agent's Copilot Studio token endpoint (from Channels > Mobile app) to get a Direct Line token with `expires_in`, then uses the Bot Framework Direct Line 3.0 API (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/publication-connect-bot-to-custom-application)
Microsoft warns never to put the Direct Line secret in client code (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/publication-connect-bot-to-custom-application)

The Microsoft 365 Agents SDK is the alternative SDK path to Direct Line for connecting a custom app to standard-harness agents (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/publication-connect-bot-to-custom-application)

Since October 2026 Copilot Studio no longer allows new WhatsApp connections through the Azure Communication Services channel; existing connections keep working (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/whats-new)

The Microsoft 365 Agents SDK is a multichannel conversational-agent framework that works with any AI service, in C# (.NET 8), JavaScript (Node 18+) and Python, with repos `microsoft/Agents-for-net`, `Agents-for-js` and `Agents-for-python` (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/agents-sdk/agents-sdk-overview ; https://github.com/microsoft/Agents)
The npm `@microsoft/agents-hosting` package is at 1.10.1 (https://registry.npmjs.org/@microsoft/agents-hosting/latest)

Agents SDK Python packages include `microsoft-agents-hosting-core`, `microsoft-agents-hosting-aiohttp`, `microsoft-agents-hosting-fastapi`, `microsoft-agents-hosting-msteams`, `microsoft-agents-authentication-msal` and `microsoft-agents-copilotstudio-client` (a client for Copilot Studio agents) (https://github.com/microsoft/Agents-for-python)
The Agents-for-python repo targets Python 3.10+, which conflicts with Learn's stated 3.9-3.11 (https://github.com/microsoft/Agents-for-python)

The Microsoft Agent 365 SDK is separate from the Microsoft 365 Agents SDK and doesn't build or host agents; it adds Entra agent identity, governed Work IQ MCP tooling and notifications to agents built on any framework (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-agent-365/developer/agent-365-sdk)
The Agent 365 SDK works with agents built on frameworks including the Claude Agent SDK, OpenAI Agents SDK and LangChain (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-agent-365/developer/agent-365-sdk)
The Agent 365 SDK supports agents built on the OpenAI Agents SDK (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-agent-365/developer/agent-365-sdk)
The Agent 365 SDK supports agents built on LangChain (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-agent-365/developer/agent-365-sdk)

Agent 365 SDK packages include `@microsoft/agents-a365-tooling-extensions-claude`, `@microsoft/agents-a365-tooling`, `microsoft-agents-a365-tooling-extensions-openai` and `Microsoft.Agents.A365.Tooling` (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-agent-365/developer/agent-365-sdk)
The Agent 365 Observability SDK packages are deprecated in favour of the Microsoft OpenTelemetry Distro (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-agent-365/developer/agent-365-sdk)
Agent 365 notifications and agent user accounts (own mailbox) are limited to tenants in the Frontier preview program (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-agent-365/developer/agent-365-sdk)

Custom MCP servers can be registered through the 'bring your own' (BYO) process and governed in the Microsoft 365 admin center Agents > Tools registry, which is the source of truth for which MCP servers a tenant can use (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-agent-365/tooling-servers-overview)
The Agents > Tools registry governs BYO MCP servers for Agent 365 (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-agent-365/tooling-servers-overview)

facts.fact: Synced Copilot connectors index content into Microsoft Graph through the Graph connectors API, configured by tenant admins or self-serve by users (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/connectors/overview)

Federated Copilot connectors fetch live through MCP without indexing and are read-only, with write actions announced for early October 2026 (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/connectors/overview)
Copilot connectors come as synced or federated, and there are 100+ prebuilt connectors (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/connectors/overview)
Power Platform custom connectors accept OpenAPI 2.0 only (no OpenAPI 3.0) or a Postman collection (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/connectors/custom-connectors/faq)

The custom connector definition file must be under 1 MB, and auth can be OAuth 2.0, API key or Basic; the client-credentials grant isn't supported (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/connectors/custom-connectors/faq)

Since February 2024, OAuth custom connectors use a per-connector redirect URI, and older connectors that used the global redirect URI must be updated (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/connectors/custom-connectors/)

The connector reference lists the certified MCP servers alongside the standard connectors (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/connectors/connector-reference/ ; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-agent-365/tooling-servers-overview)
Graph change notifications and delta queries are Microsoft's recommended alternative to polling (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/throttling)
The AI Interactions and AI Insights change-notification APIs (preview) stream Copilot interaction events (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/copilot-apis-overview)

JDBC/ODBC drivers aren't the main access path; Dataverse is reached through the OData Web API, the SDKs and MCP `read_query` (Dataverse SQL `SELECT`), and the Dataverse TDS endpoint wasn't researched (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/maker/data-platform/data-platform-mcp)

`pac` installs on Windows via the VS Code extension, the Windows MSI, or the .NET tool `dotnet tool install --global Microsoft.PowerApps.CLI.Tool` (.NET 10 recommended) (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/developer/cli/introduction ; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/developer/howto/install-cli-net-tool)

With only the .NET tool install of `pac`, `pac data`, `pac package deploy` and `pac package show` are unavailable even on Windows (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/developer/howto/install-cli-net-tool)

Current `pac` version is 2.15.1 (NuGet `Microsoft.PowerApps.CLI.Tool`, published 2026-11-12), and the .NET tool installs to `%USERPROFILE%\.dotnet\tools` (https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.PowerApps.CLI.Tool ; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/developer/howto/install-cli-net-tool)

`pac auth create` creates an authentication profile stored on the machine: the basic form is interactive, `--environment` picks the target, `--deviceCode` works in headless shells, WSL2 and Codespaces, `--applicationId`/`--clientSecret`/`--tenant` sign in as a service principal, `--managedIdentity` uses DefaultAzureCredential, `--githubFederated` and `--azureDevOpsFederated` enable OIDC, and `--cloud` accepts `UsGov`, `UsGovHigh` and other sovereign clouds (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/developer/cli/reference/auth)
Manage `pac` auth profiles with `pac auth list`, `pac auth select --index N`, `pac auth who` and `pac auth token` (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/developer/cli/reference/auth)

`pac copilot init`, `clone`, `pull`, `push` and `pack` keep a Copilot Studio agent as local files with three-way merge, and `pack` builds a solution zip for `pac solution import`; other subcommands are `list`, `publish`, `status`, `extract-template`, `create`, `quarantine` and `mcp` (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/developer/cli/reference/copilot)

`pac` has a built-in local MCP server started with `pac copilot mcp --run`, or without installing via `dnx Microsoft.PowerApps.CLI.Tool --yes copilot mcp --run`; register it in Claude Code with `claude mcp add-json pac-cli '{"type":"stdio","command":"dnx","args":["Microsoft.PowerApps.CLI.Tool","--yes","copilot","mcp","--run"]}'` (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/developer/howto/use-mcp)

Other `pac` command groups that matter for agent work are `pac solution`, `pac env`, `pac connector`, `pac connection`, `pac pipeline`, `pac admin`, `pac code` (preview; Microsoft points to the npm-based Power Apps CLI instead) and `pac pages`; preview groups include `pac copilot-studio`, `pac connectivity`, `pac governance`, `pac licensing`, `pac power-automate` and `pac resource-query` (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/developer/cli/reference/)

Non-licensed identities (application users, non-interactive users and SYSTEM) share a tenant-level pool per 24 hours: 25,000 base for Power Apps or Power Automate tenants, or 500,000 plus 5,000 per D365 USL (up to 10,000,000) for Dynamics 365 Enterprise or Professional tenants; each application user doesn't get its own pool (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/admin/api-request-limits-allocations)

Copilot Studio-triggered cloud flows share 250,000 Power Platform requests per tenant per 24 hours, the same however many Copilot Studio packs the tenant owns (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/admin/api-request-limits-allocations)

Agent flows use Copilot Credits instead of Power Platform requests and aren't subject to the 250,000-request tenant cap for Copilot Studio-triggered cloud flows (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/admin/api-request-limits-allocations)

The Power Automate 'transition period' applies higher limits per cloud flow rather than per user (Premium 200,000 per flow, Process 500,000); a phased rollout starting April 2027 switches to per-user limits, which can throttle flows that work today (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/admin/api-request-limits-allocations)
Power Automate caps every flow at 100,000 requests per five minutes, whatever the licence (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/admin/api-request-limits-allocations)

Dataverse service protection limits apply per user per web server: 6,000 requests and 1,200 seconds of execution time per 5-minute sliding window, plus 52 concurrent requests; exceeding them returns HTTP 429 with `Retry-After` (error codes `0x80072322`, `0x80072321`, `0x80072326`) (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/api-limits)
Dataverse batches hold up to 1,000 operations but don't get around entitlement limits (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/api-limits)

facts.fact: Dataverse search (`api/search`) is throttled at one request per second per user (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/api-limits)

A Power Automate cloud flow run lasts at most 30 days, synchronous outbound and inbound requests time out at 120 seconds (so use async patterns), and messages max out at 100 MB, or 1 GB with chunking (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-automate/limits-and-config)
A flow with no trigger activity for 90 days might be turned off unless its owner has a premium or capacity licence (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-automate/limits-and-config)

In Power Automate and Power Apps, each custom connector connection gets 10,000 requests per minute, and a user can create up to 50 custom connectors on a per-user plan (1 on free or seeded plans) (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/connectors/custom-connectors/faq)
Logic Apps allows 500 requests per minute per custom connector connection (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/connectors/custom-connectors/faq)

The Microsoft Graph global throttling limit is 130,000 requests per 10 seconds per app across all tenants, service-specific limits apply below it, and throttled requests get 429 with `Retry-After` (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/throttling-limits ; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/throttling)
Throttled requests inside a Graph JSON batch fail individually and aren't retried automatically by the SDKs (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/throttling)

Copilot Retrieval API limits: up to 200 requests per hour per user, `queryString` at most 1,500 characters, `maximumNumberOfResults` max 25, and each request reads one data source (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/api/ai-services/retrieval/overview)

Retrieval API results are unordered, and malformed KQL in `filterExpression` silently runs unscoped (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/api/ai-services/retrieval/overview)

Retrieval API permissions needed are `Files.Read.All` and `Sites.Read.All`, or `ExternalItem.Read.All` for connectors (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/api/ai-services/retrieval/overview)

Declarative agents always inject up to five plugins into the prompt and with more than five match plugins semantically on plugin descriptions; response quality may degrade above about 10 functions or tools, and large tool output is truncated (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/overview-plugins)

Standard-harness Copilot Credit rates: classic answer 1; generative answer 2; agent action (including triggers, topic transitions and each computer-use step) 5; tenant graph grounding 10; agent flow actions 13 per 100 actions; basic AI tools 1 per 10 responses; standard AI tools 15 per 10 responses; premium (reasoning) tools 10 per 1,000 tokens; content processing 8 per page (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/requirements-messages-management)

Reasoning-model agents pay the feature rate plus 10 credits per 1,000 billed tokens; every model call in a turn counts, only prompt-cache reads are free, and Microsoft's example has one follow-up question costing 141 credits, or about 461 credits in a new conversation (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/requirements-messages-management)

Employee-facing agent usage by Microsoft 365 Copilot-licensed users isn't charged, except computer use, agent flows not started by the 'When an agent calls the flow' trigger, and flows called by autonomous agents (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/requirements-messages-management)
Computer use is excluded from the no-charge rule for Microsoft 365 Copilot-licensed employees (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/requirements-messages-management)

Agents are blocked at 125% of prepaid capacity unless pay-as-you-go is linked, mid-conversation, with the message "This agent is currently unavailable. It has reached its usage limit."; agent flow runs are blocked separately as soon as the environment has no credits (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/requirements-messages-management)

Microsoft Copilot and Customer Conversation harness agents use a different usage-based billing model whose rates live on a separate page (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/harnesses-overview)
Customer Conversation harness agents use a different usage-based billing model from the standard harness (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/harnesses-overview)
Copilot Studio MCP and A2A channel use consumes Copilot Credits (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/publication-channels-mcp-agent-to-agent)

Dataverse MCP `search_data` is billed per use in Copilot Credits, and all other Dataverse MCP tools are billed at the basic text and generative AI rate per 10 responses (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/maker/data-platform/data-platform-mcp)

In parent/child tenants the Work IQ token issuer must be the user's home tenant, otherwise calls fail with `400 AuthenticationError: "Error authenticating with resource"`; register the app as `AzureADMultipleOrgs` (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/work-iq/api-overview)
